nodes.label: laptop memory - the corroboration probe verdict

Frozen copy taken 2026-08-03 of the laptop's live memory file - evidence of what this machine believed at that date, listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 7. 2026-07-29, run offline on the committed baseline (detCUR 0.7339, gold-100): rare-tag corroboration is a real signal but a redundant discriminator, and the verdict binds this operationalization - capped shared-tag counts against top-ranked seeds - not the user's corroboration concept. The signal is real, beating random territory fill by +0.029..+0.041 with p <= 0.003 on all tails and a stage-1 AUC of 0.64 at the best config. It fails the pre-declared bar: corroboration minus description-distance is <= +0.014 and n.s. at every tail, because description distance already expresses whatever event structure capped tag-sharing reaches. Rareness is not where the event information lives - AUC rises monotonically with degree cap, and degree <= 5 tags miss 82% of missed-gold chunks entirely. Oracle headroom is quantified at +0.2125 recall from a 10-slot in-territory swap, 0.7339 to 0.9463, so the territory contains the gain and no found discriminator captures more than about 5% of it. The stage-3 combination follow-up: complementarity is REAL, with a per-question oracle chooser worth +0.041 to a ceiling of 0.7845, but INACCESSIBLE to question-independent rules - score fusion -0.005, rank fusion +0.005, both p about 0.7, fitted per-type routing only +0.011. Verdict: corr x desc fusion CLOSED; a gain requires a new per-question regime signal
